reply_text:
You're right, and the memory note was the same reflex again. Here is what I think went wrong and what would make the work progressive.

**What went wrong.** I gated each click on "is the fix I dispatched loaded?", not on "what will the machine do next, and is that new?" Before click 20 I wrote that it would probably re-select the same target, and I fired it anyway because my plan said click 20 follows the parallel-asks handoff. It wasn't only click 20:

- **Click 17** asked about a target with no class, when kimi-3 had already reported that cause for M-formal-patterns.
- **Click 18** ran a classifier I had never called live. One probe in the serving JVM would have shown every target as `:unknown`, and I ran that probe only after the click failed.
- **Click 20** repeated click 19.

So three of the last five clicks found out something I could have known without firing.

**What I think "progressive" needs.** Both parts are checks in code, so neither depends on me remembering:

1. **Operator side: a dry-run before every click.** Run the decision in the serving JVM without dispatching, and print the target, cascade and ask target it would choose. `wm_click.sh` refuses to fire if that matches an earlier click that ended in failure and nothing that failure named has changed. I haven't confirmed the decision can be called without side effects; that is the first thing to check.
2. **A stated claim per click.** Before firing, I write down the one capability this click is expected to show that no earlier click showed, derived from the dry-run. If I can't name one, there's no click. Afterwards the claim is marked shown or not shown in the proof's record.
3. **Machine side: selection reads its own refusals.** This is the repair I should have made after click 19.

**Two questions where your view changes what I build:**

- **What should a typed author refusal become?** The narrow version holds back that target-and-cascade pair until the mission document or its interpretations change. The fuller version turns the refusal into selectable work: the author said the I1–I6 audit is missing, so the audit becomes a want the machine can pick. I think the fuller version is the progressive one, since the narrow one only moves the machine on to the next target.
- **Does the dry-run count against your click budget?** I'd say no, since it dispatches nothing, but it's your budget.

I'd also delete the memory note I just wrote, since the check in `wm_click.sh` replaces it.
